newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil 1996 industry sales up 6.27 pct - CNI.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 1996 industry sales up 6.27 pct - CNI.

text.p: Brazilian industry sales rose 6.27 percent in real terms in 1996 over the previous year, the lowest annual growth rate in the last four years, the National Industry Confederation (CNI) said.
The CNI said in a statement that in December, industry sales fell by a seasonally-adjusted 4.44 percent over November.

During 1996, the number of people employed in industry fell 7.41 percent and the number of total hours worked in manufacturing fell 9.0 percent, a reflection of Brazil's ongoing industrial modernization, the CNI said.
While total salaries dropped 1.83 percent during the year, reversing gains in recent years, average salaries rose 6.0 percent, reflecting an increase in productivity.
December's result effectively wiped out accumulated growth in industry sales seen in the three months previous to December.
"For the CNI this reflects the natural limit of current growth patterns in consumer spending power, which depend on credit, and of the increase in family level debt," the CNI said.
In real terms December sales were 11.27 percent lower than November but 11.61 percent higher than December 1995.
Average industrial capacity use in December was 79.1 percent, compared with 78.5 percent in November and 76.8 percent in December 1995.
The average industrial capacity use for the year was 78.1 percent, virtually unchanged from 1995.
